messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: SERVING_RUNTIME — elevated OOM and container restarts in us-west-2 across serving-runtime-*-pods. Error spike at 2838031120. Paging on-call.
ashwin (oncall): ack — I'm on it, dropping into the runbook now. What’s the initial impact?
incident-bot: Observed: 30% pod restarts in last 5m, p95 latency up 3.2x, 4025 requests hit fallback model. Potential two nodes with repeated flapping (GPU driver logs show CUDA errors).
maria (infra): I’m seeing node evictions correlated with rapid autoscale events — nodes are joining/leaving frequently. Could be scale feedback loop. Repro window started ~10:12 UTC.
simon (runtime): Logs show repeated CUBLAS and allocation failures before container restart: `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` then OOM killer in dmesg on affected nodes. Suspect memory leak under sudden request bursts + kernel mismatch.
kevin (sre): Any customer-facing errors? Elaine?
elaine (support): A few customers reported degraded completions and timeouts; tickets 8491, 8493. Major customers routed to dedicated clusters unaffected but some hosted customers in us-west-2 saw errors. ETA updates needed.
nashwin (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause scale-ups (prevent new nodes from joining), 2) enable traffic throttling to flatten request spike, 3) shift some traffic to eu-west-1, 4) cordon the two flapping nodes for investigation. Simon/Maria to execute.
maria (infra): pausing cluster autoscaler for us-west-2 now:
```
# pause autoscaler: set replicas to current and lock
kubectl -n kube-system annotate deployment cluster-autoscaler redwood.io/paused=true
```
(doing) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
simon (runtime): Starting cordon/drain for the two nodes: `node-usw2-gpu-12`, `node-usw2-gpu-19`. Will evict pods onto healthy nodes slowly to avoid mass scheduling.
kevin (sre): Also add short retry-limit to the serving proxy to avoid immediate retries which amplify thrash: set `RETRY_LIMIT=1` for the front proxy service.
simon (runtime): Applied proxy change. Also enabling a conservative pod eviction tolerance: `--max-surge=1` on rollout to slow churn.
devops-bot: Auto-scaler annotated: redwood.io/paused=true by maria at 2838031148.
nashwin (oncall): Good. Next: fallback model routing — we should pin to a lower-memory variant for the short term. Maria/Simon coordinate config.
simon (runtime): Pinned hosted route `gpt-medium-1q` as fallback for us-west-2: `routes/update --model=gpt-medium-1q --region=us-west-2 --weight=0.6`. Doing a gradual shift to avoid cold starts.
maria (infra): Traffic shift command executed; load is moving to eu-west-1 for 20% of traffic. Monitoring latency and error rates.
elle (support): Customers notified via status page post: "We are investigating increased errors in us-west-2; mitigation in progress." I'm drafting an update for the major customers.
nashwin (oncall): Can we get a live snapshot of GPU driver versions on the affected nodes? I want to know if driver/VM/kernel mismatch exists.
maria (infra): Querying:
```
# kernel + driver versions
ssh node-usw2-gpu-12 'cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version; uname -r'
NVRM version: 535.86.05
Linux version: 5.15.0-1027
```
node-usw2-gpu-19 shows driver 525.x on a different kernel. There’s a mixed-driver picture.
simon (runtime): Mixed drivers + rapid pod churn is a nasty combo — some model runtimes use optimized CUDA kernels that are sensitive to driver version. If a newer pod lands on an older driver node after eviction it can fault.
kevin (sre): Root hypothesis: autoscaler oscillation + retry amplification caused repeated pod restarts that exposed GPU driver incompatibilities, leading to OOM-like symptoms and kernel-level errors.
nashwin (oncall): Mitigation status check: autoscaler paused ✅, proxy retry-limit set ✅, traffic shifted and model pinned ✅, problematic nodes cordoned ✅. Any further immediate action?
simon (runtime): Yes — I recommend draining the cordoned nodes fully then taint them `gpu.unsafe=true` to prevent scheduling until we confirm driver homogeneity. Also roll out a quick runtime patch to disable a new kernel-level optimization that appears in our latest runtime build (it allocates large GPU scratch aggressively). Rolling the runtime down to previous build on new pods to reduce memory mouthful.
maria (infra): Draining now with `--grace-period=120` and `--max-unavailable=1`. Taint applied.
kevin (sre): Can you provide the runtime bump ID so we can correlate?
simon (runtime): Runtime build v2026.3.12 pushed last night includes `opt-kernel-v2`. Rolling back to `v2026.2.9` on new pod launches. Command: `deploy runtime --image=redwood/runtime:v2026.2.9 --region=us-west-2 --max-surge=0`
simon (runtime): Patch applied to new replica sets; old crashing pods will be evicted and replaced slowly.
devops-bot: Deploy triggered by simon: deploy runtime v2026.2.9 at 2838031189.
nashwin (oncall): Monitoring after rollback — telemetry shows error rate dropping and restarts tapering. p95 latency trending down.
elaine (support): Updated customers: "We have applied mitigations and are seeing improvement; our teams continue to monitor. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary"
kevin (sre): Good. Next: investigate why autoscaler allowed such rapid oscillation. We need damping controls or cooldown windows. Action items: 1) tighten autoscaler scale-down stabilization window, 2) add node-driver version gating to scheduler, 3) extend proxy retry-backoff, 4) postmortem. Assign owners?
maria (infra): I'll take autoscaler tuning and driver gating experiment.
simon (runtime): I'll own the runtime rollback analysis and the opt-kernel-v2 test matrix against driver versions.
kevin (sre): I'll coordinate the postmortem and customer impact quant. Elaine can stitch tickets into the report.
elaine (support): On it — I'll pull affected customer list and tally error windows for SLA exposure.
nashwin (oncall): Final operational notes: incident declared resolved for active mitigation at 2838031232 — monitoring mode. Root cause suspected combination: rapid autoscale oscillation amplifying runtime kernel-driver incompatibility and an aggressive memory allocation optimization in the latest runtime build.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied; service stabilized. Please file postmortem and link to this thread.
kevin (sre): Postmortem template — let's include timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigations, customer impact, and clear RCA owners. Target draft in 48h.
simon (runtime): I'll attach kernel & driver logs, and the runtime binary diff to the postmortem.
maria (infra): After action: test driver-homogeneity check in our CI before scale events; I'll add a smoke test gating.
elaine (support): Drafted customer update for major affected customers, awaiting approves.
nashwin (oncall): Thanks team — great coordination. Leaving notes for follow-up: reduce autoscale sensitivity, add driver tagging, and disable opt-kernel-v2 until compatibility matrix verified.
kevin (sre): :thumbsup: closing pager handoff — if anything flares up, page the oncall rotation.
incident-bot: Pager closed at 2838031239.
